name: Target
oneLiner: An internship search copilot for my classmates: build your candidate file once, reuse it at every step.
problem: My classmates kept asking how I land internships. With a chatbot they start from zero every time: a generic CV, shallow prep, nothing to show. Each step alone is easy; what changes the outcome is one candidate file reused everywhere, and a method with guardrails.
built: A candidate file: a short interview turns your experience into an evidence bank, one fact per proof, each one validated by you.
Per application: a targeted CV ("you sell X, they buy Y"), a research prompt whose sources get checked, an HR interview kit and a project brief for the manager round.
A tracker with CSV import and a Chrome extension to save offers in one click.
proof: Success rule set before launch: if 2 testers out of 3 land an interview within six weeks, it moves to v2; 1 out of 3, I change one variable; none, I stop and find where it breaks.
Product rule learned in testing: the code ends the interview, not the model (eight questions, a visible counter), after one session ran to thirty questions.
